topIssues.title: op-reth: validate fork-specific block-header extraData
topIssues.author: asdv23
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

At `develop@a6a088325deebbe6cad74db395b9a079669580b6`, `OpBeaconConsensus::validate_header` only applies the generic 32-byte `extraData` length cap.

It therefore accepts non-genesis pre-Holocene headers with non-empty `extraData`, and malformed Holocene/Jovian encodings whose length is at most 32 bytes. The OP specifications require empty pre-Holocene `extraData`, exactly 9 bytes with version 0 during Holocene, and exactly 17 bytes with version 1 from Jovian onward.

The decoders updated by #21292 enforce the fork-specific encoding rules, but they are only reached later when a header is used as the parent for base-fee calculation. They do not validate the current header. This delays rejection by one block and differs from op-geth, which calls `ValidateOptimismExtraData` while processing `engine_newPayload`.

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Construct an `OpChainSpec` with the relevant fork activation.
2. Construct a sealed header that is otherwise valid but has invalid `extraData`.
3. Call `OpBeaconConsensus::validate_header`.
4. Observe `Ok(())` for examples such as:
   - non-empty pre-Holocene `extraData` on a non-genesis header;
   - empty or wrong-version Holocene `extraData`;
   - a 9-byte Holocene encoding after Jovian activation.

**Expected behavior**

Match the OP execution specification and op-geth `ValidateOptimismExtraData` behavior:

- allow arbitrary pre-Holocene `extraData` only for the configured genesis header;
- require empty `extraData` on other pre-Holocene blocks;
- validate the exact Holocene and Jovian formats at their respective activation timestamps.

**Environment Information:**

- Repository: `ethereum-optimism/optimism`
- Commit: `a6a088325deebbe6cad74db395b9a079669580b6`
- Component: `rust/op-reth/crates/consensus`
- Operating system: independent of OS; reproduced by direct consensus validation

**Configurations:**

Default `OpBeaconConsensus` with timestamp-activated Holocene/Jovian chain specifications. No special node flags are required.

**Logs:**

No runtime logs are required. The direct `validate_header` call unexpectedly returns `Ok(())` for the malformed headers above.

**Additional context**

Related work covers adjacent but incomplete parts of the behavior:

- #18951 / #21292 added validation to the op-alloy decoders.
- ethereum-optimism/op-geth#743 added the complete op-geth header validation.
- paradigmxyz/reth#20858 tightened payload-attribute validation, not block-header validation.

The proposed fix belongs in the consensus layer so every import path applies the same rule.

topPRs.title: op-reth: validate fork-specific header extra data
topPRs.author: asdv23
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- validate non-genesis pre-Holocene block headers have empty `extraData`
- validate exact Holocene and Jovian encodings with the existing op-alloy decoders
- preserve arbitrary pre-Holocene `extraData` for the configured genesis header

## Context

`OpBeaconConsensus::validate_header` previously applied only the generic 32-byte length cap. As a result, op-reth accepted malformed current headers that op-geth rejects in `engine_newPayload`; decoder validation only happened later when the block became a parent for base-fee calculation.

Closes #22957.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-consensus` (26 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-consensus --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check -p reth-optimism-consensus --no-default-features`
- `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check`

topPRs.title: op-interop-mon: clean up partial initialization safely
topPRs.author: grandpig
topPRs.body:
<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

<!--
A clear and concise description of the features you're adding in this pull request.
-->

Clean up partially initialized `InteropMonitorService` instances when construction fails.

Both service constructors previously called `Start` after an initialization error:

```go
return nil, errors.Join(err, ms.Start(ctx))
```

This could start finders, updaters, and the metric collector after construction had already failed. Since the constructor returns a nil service, the caller would have no way to stop these background tasks or any HTTP servers started earlier in initialization.

The constructors now call Stop on initialization failure instead.

This also makes partial cleanup safe when metrics are disabled. The metric collector is only created when metrics are enabled, but Stop previously called ms.collector.Stop() unconditionally, causing a nil-pointer panic.

The logger is initialized before running either initialization path so cleanup is also safe when the CLI constructor fails before initFromClients.



**Tests**

<!--
Please describe any tests you've added. If you've added no tests, or left important behavior untested, please explain why not.
-->

`cd op-interop-mon && just test`

`go test -race ./op-interop-mon/monitor -run 'TestInteropMonitor(StopWithMetricsDisabled|InitFailureCleansUpServers|PartialInitCleanupIsNilSafe|CLIInitFailureCleanupIsNilSafe)$' -count=1`

topPRs.title: docs: remove CLAUDE.md symlinks in favor of AGENTS.md
topPRs.author: jarrensj
topPRs.body:
## Description

Removes the eight `CLAUDE.md` symlinks that point at a sibling `AGENTS.md`: the repo root, `.circleci`, `.github`, `op-acceptance-tests`, `op-node/rollup/derive`, `packages/contracts-bedrock`, `rust`, and `rust/kona/crates/protocol`. As of [Claude Code v2.1.277](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.277), Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` directly when a directory has no `CLAUDE.md`, so the aliases no longer do anything. The `AGENTS.md` symlinks into `docs/ai/` are unchanged.

References updated:

- `.claude/agents/go-code-reviewer.md` now points reviewers at `AGENTS.md` instead of `CLAUDE.md`.
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/kontrol/scripts/common.sh` no longer removes the `CLAUDE.md` alias from its temp copy, since it will not exist.

Left alone on purpose: `rust/kona/CLAUDE.md`, which is a real file rather than an alias, and the mentions of `CLAUDE.md` in the prompt-injection guidance in `AGENTS.md` and the watch-reviews skill, which still apply to that file.

## Tests

`git ls-files -s | grep 120000 | grep CLAUDE.md` returns nothing after the change. No Go, Rust, or Solidity code is touched.
